\begin{lemma}[Rotation sensitivity and noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_eq_stability}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_eq_stability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability_indicator_measure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianCombination, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in[0,\pi]$. If
$\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbf 1_A$ is the
indicator of $A$, then the probability that a standard Gaussian vector and its rotation
by angle $\theta$ with an independent standard Gaussian vector disagree on membership in
$A$ equals $2\bigl(\gamma_n(A)-\operatorname{Stab}_{\cos\theta}(\mathbf 1_A)\bigr)$,
where $\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\mathbb E[f(X)f(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)]$ for
independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$.
\end{lemma}
